item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau helped secure visa for fugitive Polish minister
item.description:
U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau personally directed senior officials to facilitate a visa for Zbigniew Ziobro, a fugitive former Polish justice minister facing 26 criminal charges, enabling him to flee Hungary for the United States, according to a Reuters exclusive report citing three people familiar with the matter.

Landau instructed officials from the State Department's Consular Affairs Bureau to order the U.S. embassy in Budapest to issue the visa, describing the matter as "a national security issue," one source told Reuters. One source described the document as a journalist visa, a characterization that aligns with earlier Polish media reports suggesting Ziobro may be working as a correspondent for TV Republika, a right-wing Polish broadcaster. The sources told Reuters they were unaware of any involvement by President Donald Trump, and it remained unclear what role Secretary of State Marco Rubio played.

item.title: Iran details peace proposal demanding reparations, end of blockade
item.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed on Tuesday that Tehran's latest peace proposal to the United States includes the lifting of sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian funds, and an end to the U.S. naval blockade, according to a Reuters report citing Iran's state news agency IRNA. The proposal also calls for a ceasefire on all fronts, including Lebanon, the exit of U.S. forces from areas near Iran, and reparations for destruction caused by the war.

The terms appear largely unchanged from Iran's previous offer, which President Donald Trump rejected last week as "garbage".

item.title: China secretly trained 200 Russian troops now fighting in Ukraine, Reuters reports
item.description: China's armed forces covertly trained approximately 200 Russian military personnel in China late last year, with some of those soldiers having since returned to fight in Ukraine, according to an exclusive report by Reuters. The revelation, published as Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marks a new threshold in military cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Iran offers to send enriched uranium to Russia in amended US peace plan
item.description: Iran has proposed transferring its stockpile of approximately 400 kilograms of highly enriched uranium to Russia rather than the United States, according to leaked details of Tehran's amended peace proposal reported by Al Arabiya on Monday. The offer marks a shift in Iran's negotiating posture and comes as President Donald Trump paused a planned military strike to allow diplomacy to continue.

item.title: Russia claims Ukraine plans drone strikes from Latvia, threatens Riga
item.description:
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) claimed on Monday that Ukraine is preparing to launch drone strikes against Russian targets from Latvian military bases, an accusation swiftly rejected by both Riga and Kyiv as disinformation.

The SVR alleged that soldiers from Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces had already been deployed to military installations in Latvia, and that Kyiv intended to use Latvian territory — not just airspace — as a launching platform for attacks, calculating that shorter flight distances would increase the effectiveness of strikes. The agency added a veiled threat, stating that "the coordinates of decision-making centers on Latvian territory are well known" and that NATO membership "will not protect those who aid terrorists from just retribution".

item.title: Google I/O 2026 kicks off today with Gemini AI updates
item.description: Google is rolling out a slate of updates to its Gemini AI assistant just as Google I/O 2026 kicks off today, May 19, at Shoreline Amphitheatre in Mountain View, California. Among the most notable additions is a "thinking level" control that lets users choose how much reasoning the model applies to their prompts — addressing a longstanding complaint about fixed reasoning modes.

item.title: NATO weighs naval mission in Hormuz as strait nears four months of closure
item.description: NATO is actively discussing a potential naval deployment to help secure commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz if the waterway remains blocked into early July, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing a senior alliance official. The discussions mark a shift for the alliance, which earlier this year refused to participate in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports but now faces mounting pressure as the disruption to one of the world's most critical shipping routes approaches its fourth month.

item.title: Trump says US may strike Iran again within days
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the United States may need to attack Iran again, revealing he was just an hour away from ordering a new strike before he postponed the operation. The remarks came a day after Trump called off what he described as a "very major attack" that had been scheduled for Tuesday, at the request of Gulf allies who said diplomatic negotiations were making progress.

item.title: NATO has no Hormuz mission plans, top commander says
item.description: NATO's top military commander said Tuesday that the alliance has no plans in motion for an operation in the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring that any such mission would first require political consensus among all 32 member states — a threshold that remains far from being met.

item.title: Trump's Gaza board warns of funding gap in UN report
item.description:
President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has warned that the gap between funding pledges and actual disbursements for Gaza's reconstruction must be closed "with urgency," according to a May 15 report to the United Nations Security Council viewed by Reuters on Tuesday.

The board, established to oversee Trump's plan to rebuild the war-shattered territory, said that funds committed but not yet disbursed represent "the difference between a framework that exists on paper and one that delivers on the ground for the people of Gaza". While the report confirmed that $17 billion remains pledged, it did not disclose how much has actually been received or quantify the shortfall.

item.title: Drone strike kills 28 at crowded market in Sudan
item.description:
A drone strike hit a bustling market in the town of Ghabesh in Sudan's West Kordofan state on Tuesday, killing at least 28 people and wounding dozens more, according to local rights monitors.

The attack, reported by the Emergency Lawyers group, marks the latest in a relentless wave of drone warfare against civilian targets in Sudan's Kordofan region, where fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has intensified in recent months.

item.title: EU reaches deal to cut US import duties ahead of Trump's tariff deadline
item.description:
European Union negotiators reached a provisional agreement early Wednesday on legislation to eliminate import duties on US goods, clearing a critical hurdle in the bloc's race to comply with President Donald Trump's July 4 ultimatum before tariffs on European exports escalate sharply.

The deal, struck after a final round of trilogue talks between the European Parliament and the Council of the EU in Strasbourg, finalizes the legislative framework needed to implement the Turnberry Agreement — the trade pact reached between Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025.

item.title: NATO weighs Hormuz mission as top commander confirms talks
item.description: NATO is actively discussing the possibility of deploying a military mission to the Strait of Hormuz if the critical waterway remains blocked beyond early July, according to Bloomberg reporting confirmed by alliance officials. The deliberations mark a potential turning point for the alliance, which has so far avoided direct involvement in the broader U.S.-Iran conflict.

item.title: Chile's Kast fires security minister in first cabinet shake-up
item.description: Chilean President José Antonio Kast carried out his first cabinet reshuffle on Tuesday, removing Security Minister Trinidad Steinert and Government Spokesperson Mara Sedini just over two months into his administration, in a shake-up that underscores growing unease over his government's handling of its core policy promise: fighting crime.

item.title: Putin hails 'unprecedented' Russia-China ties in Beijing talks with Xi
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Wednesday, hailing relations between the two countries as having reached an "unprecedentedly high level" and calling for a more balanced international order as trade and energy ties continue to expand.

item.title: US and Israel planned to install Ahmadinejad after Iran war began
item.description:
The United States and Israel entered the February 2026 war against Iran with a secret plan to elevate former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as the country's new leader following the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, according to a New York Times report published on May 19 citing US officials.

The revelation exposes the full scope of the regime-change ambitions underlying Operation Epic Fury, the US military campaign, and Israel's Operation Roaring Lion, which began with massive airstrikes on February 28, 2026.

item.title: Xi and Putin condemn Golden Dome at Beijing summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin used a high-profile summit in Beijing on Wednesday to jointly condemn the United States' Golden Dome missile defense program, calling it "an obvious threat to strategic stability" and warning that it risked turning outer space into a theater of war.

item.title: Samsung union suspends strike after last-minute deal
item.description: Samsung Electronics and its largest labor union reached a tentative agreement on Wednesday evening, suspending a general strike by nearly 48,000 workers that had been set to begin Thursday. The deal came after Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon personally intervened to broker a last-ditch negotiation session, stepping in hours after talks at the National Labor Relations Commission collapsed earlier in the day.

item.title: Barney Frank, gay rights pioneer in Congress, dies at 86
item.description:
Former Massachusetts Congressman Barney Frank, one of the first openly gay members of Congress and co-author of the landmark Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act, has died at age 86. His sister, Ann Lewis, confirmed the news to NBC News on Wednesday.

Frank died at his home in Ogunquit, Maine, where he had been in hospice care since late April due to congestive heart failure. He is survived by his husband, Jim Ready, whom he married in 2012.

item.title: OpenAI prepares to submit confidential IPO filing within days
item.description:
OpenAI is working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on a confidential IPO prospectus that could be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission within days, according to reports, as the ChatGPT maker accelerates its path toward what would be one of the largest public offerings in history.

The filing would come just days after a California jury unanimously dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, removing what many viewed as the most pressing legal obstacle to the company's public listing.
